examples: Take a deep breath and stay calm.
The sea is calm today.
Mom's voice is calm and soft.

more.def: Peaceful and quiet; not excited, worried, or angry.
examples: The lake was calm and smooth after the storm passed.
The pilot stayed calm during the bumpy flight.
Soft music helps me feel calm before bed.

easy.def: Colors that help an animal hide.
examples: The frog's green skin is camouflage in the grass.
A tiger's stripes are camouflage in tall grass.
The moth uses camouflage to hide on a tree.

more.def: Colors or patterns that help an animal or thing blend in with what is around it.
examples: A snowshoe hare's white fur is good camouflage in winter.
The soldiers wore green and brown camouflage in the forest.
An octopus can change color for camouflage.
The net will capture the fish.
I captured a bug in a jar.
The police captured the robber.

more.def: To catch and hold a person, animal, or thing.
examples: The photographer captured a picture of the eagle in flight.
The scientists captured the bird, tagged it, and let it go.
In the game, you capture the other team's flag to win.

easy.def: Trying hard to stay safe and not make a mistake.
examples: Be careful with the hot soup.
Be careful on the icy steps.
I am careful with my glasses.

more.def: Paying close attention so that you avoid danger or mistakes.
examples: She was careful not to step on the wet paint.
He made a careful drawing of the bird's feathers.
Be careful to check your answers before you turn in the test.

easy.def: To do something fun for a special day.
examples: We celebrate my birthday with cake.
We celebrate the new year with a party.
Let's celebrate! You lost a tooth!

more.def: To do something special or fun to mark a happy day or event.
examples: The team celebrated their win with a pizza party.
Many families celebrate holidays with special meals.
The town celebrated the opening of the new bridge.
The big puzzle is a challenge.
Tying my shoes was a challenge.
This game is a fun challenge.

more.def: Something difficult that tests your skill or strength.
examples: Climbing the steep hill was a real challenge.
Learning a new language can be a challenge.
The long math problem was a challenge for the whole class.
She has a cheerful smile.
The room is painted a cheerful yellow.
A cheerful bird sang to us.

more.def: Happy and full of good feelings.
examples: The cheerful bus driver greeted every child by name.
He stayed cheerful even though it rained on his birthday.
The nurse's cheerful voice made the patients feel better.

easy.def: What the weather is like in a place most of the time.
examples: The climate here is hot and dry.
Polar bears live in a cold climate.
The climate by the sea is wet.

more.def: The usual weather a place has over a long period of time.
examples: Penguins live in a very cold climate.
Oranges grow best in a warm, sunny climate.
Scientists study how the Earth's climate is changing.
I collect pretty rocks.
We collect shells at the beach.
The teacher collects our papers.

more.def: To gather things together, sometimes as a hobby.
examples: He collects stamps from countries all around the world.
A truck collects the trash every Tuesday.
Bees collect nectar from flowers to make honey.
My bed is so comfortable.
This chair is comfortable.
I feel comfortable in my pajamas.

more.def: Feeling relaxed and at ease, or making you feel that way.
examples: These shoes are comfortable enough to wear all day.
She felt comfortable talking to her grandmother about anything.
The hotel room was small but comfortable.

easy.def: The people who live in one place.
examples: Our community has a park and a school.
People in our community help each other.
The community garden grows beans.

more.def: A group of people who live in the same area or who share something important.
examples: The whole community helped clean up the beach.
The school is an important part of our community.
A community of ants works together to build a nest.

easy.def: To look at two things to see how they are the same or not the same.
examples: Compare the two apples. Which is bigger?
We compare our hands to see whose is bigger.
Compare the two pictures.

more.def: To look closely at two or more things to find how they are alike and different.
examples: We compared the two maps and noticed that one had more rivers.
She compared prices at two stores before buying the shoes.
In science, we compared how fast ice melts in sun and shade.
It takes courage to try new things.
The knight had a lot of courage.
It took courage to pet the big dog.

more.def: The strength to do something even though it is scary or hard.
examples: It took courage to tell the truth about what happened.
The firefighters showed great courage during the rescue.
He found the courage to try out for the school play.
Let's create a picture with paint.
We create a castle from sand.
Bees create honey.

more.def: To make or invent something that did not exist before.
examples: The students created a model of the solar system.
The author created a whole new world in her book.
Wind and water created the shapes in these rocks.
A tiny creature ran under the leaf.
A snail is a slow creature.
What creature made these tracks?

more.def: Any living animal, real or imaginary.
examples: Strange creatures live at the bottom of the ocean.
The tide pool was full of tiny sea creatures.
The dragon is a creature found only in stories.
The curious kitten looked in the box.
I am curious about what is in the bag.
The curious baby touches everything.

more.def: Eager to learn or find out about something.
examples: He was curious about how airplanes stay up in the sky.
Curious visitors gathered around the strange machine.
She was curious to know where the trail led.
